llm.summary: The skill broadly matches its stated purpose (an agent 'OS') but a few mismatches and persistence behaviors (cron jobs, heavy use of exec) are disproportionate or under-specified — review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (a full 'AI Persona OS') aligns with the included templates, policies, and helper scripts — the bundle is coherent for provisioning an agent workspace. However SKILL.md repeatedly calls the 'openclaw' CLI and prescribes adding cron jobs and gateway-config changes while the registry metadata declares no required binaries or config paths. That mismatch (expectation of a platform CLI and system-level actions vs. no declared requirements) is an engineering/information gap worth flagging.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions explicitly tell the agent to run many shell commands via exec (create ~/workspace directories, copy templates, add scheduled jobs, run setup and audit scripts). Those instructions stay within the 'set up and maintain an agent' purpose, but they grant the skill broad discretion to read/write files under the user's home and to schedule recurring jobs. The SKILL.md does claim safety guardrails (never overwrite without asking, security guidance), but the agent-driven-first-run behavior (immediately run setup when files missing) could lead to a lot of automated changes if the agent has exec privileges.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads are included — the skill package includes templates and local scripts only. No external URL downloads or package installs were specified in the provided metadata, which reduces supply-chain risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential, which is consistent with a local workspace provisioning tool. That said, the instructions recommend modifying gateway configs and adding cron jobs (which may implicitly require platform tokens or CLI access). Because the manifest doesn't declare those requirements, an operator may be surprised when the agent attempts actions that need additional permissions or credentials.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Although always:false, SKILL.md instructs creating scheduled jobs (openclaw cron add) and persistent workspace files (.learnings/, memory/, cron tasks). Those scheduled jobs will cause recurring autonomous activity (heartbeat, daily/weekly reviews, audits). That creates persistent behavior and an ongoing execution surface; it increases blast radius if scripts perform unexpected network activity. The skill doesn't declare automatic persistence in metadata, so the creation of persistent cron tasks without explicit pre-declaration is a noteworthy risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing or running this skill:

1) Expect the skill to run many shell commands via exec and to create files under ~/workspace — back up your workspace first or test in a disposable account/workspace.
2) The SKILL.md uses the 'openclaw' CLI and schedules cron tasks, but the registry metadata lists no required binaries; confirm the needed CLI/tools are present and understand what privileged tokens/configs they'll use.
3) Review the included scripts (especially scripts/setup-wizard.sh and scripts/security-audit.sh) for any network activity, external endpoints, or commands that could exfiltrate data or change system-wide settings before approving exec prompts.
4) Be aware the skill will create recurring jobs (daily/weekly/cron) that cause autonomous runs; if you want to limit persistence, don't approve cron creation or edit cron templates to run in an isolated session first.
5) Verify gateway configuration changes (requireMention settings) and any instructions that would alter shared-channel behavior — those may require platform credentials or admin rights not declared by the skill.
6) If you lack the time or skills to audit scripts yourself: run the setup in an isolated VM/container, or decline installation until the author documents exact external calls, required binaries, and the precise commands that will be executed by the agent.
